mainTopic: A stolen חטאת and a thief's הקדש; the law of סיקריקון; the start of the story of קמצא and בר קמצא
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב יהודה's reason for the testimony about a stolen חטאת. If the theft is publicly known, the חטאת does not atone, so that people will not say the מזבח eats stolen goods. The גמרא tests this reason twice against the wording of the משנה. In both cases it shows that the wording fits רב יהודה as well as עולא. רבא then challenges עולא's view that יאוש alone does not give the thief ownership. He brings a ברייתא in which a thief who made a stolen animal הקדש gets כרת for slaughtering it outside the מקדש. רב שיזבי answers 'כרת מדבריהם.' רבא explains this to mean that the חכמים placed the animal in the thief's ownership, and he rules that this ownership begins only from the הקדש, so the sinner does not profit. A new משנה follows about land bought from a סיקריקון, an extortionist, and traces how the law changed over three stages. The גמרא explains, using three Roman decrees, why that law did not apply during the war. Finally, רבי יוחנן opens the stories of the destruction, beginning with the tale of קמצא and בר קמצא.

steps.title: The reason a known stolen offering does not atone
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's explanation finishes: if it is publicly known that the חטאת was stolen, it does not bring כפרה, so people will not say the מזבח eats stolen goods.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did the חכמים say that once it is known, it does not atone? So that people will not say the altar eats stolen goods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב יהודה's explanation of the testimony. He gives the reason a stolen חטאת that everyone knows about does not bring כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יהודה, the main point of the rule is the case where the theft is known. Then the offering does not atone, so the honor of the מזבח is protected. People must never think the מזבח 'eats' stolen property.

keyTerms.meaning: It became known (that the animal was stolen)
Brings atonement (כפרה)
The altar
Stolen goods

steps.whyThisMatters: This reason, the honor of the מזבח, is what the rest of the section tests against the wording of the משנה.

phrases.english: And what is the reason they said
that if it became known, it does not atone?
So that people should not say
the altar eats stolen goods.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה טַעַם אָמְרוּ נוֹדְעָה אֵינָהּ מְכַפֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יהודה's explanation, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stolen חטאת whose theft is publicly known does not atone, so that people will not say the מזבח consumes stolen property.

steps.title: According to רב יהודה, why mention only a חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: For עולא, mentioning a חטאת makes sense because כהנים eat it. For רב יהודה, the concern about the מזבח should apply even more to an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to עולא, that is why it teaches a חטאת. But according to רב יהודה, why specifically a חטאת? Even an עולה should be included too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה. If the worry is about the מזבח, why does the teaching mention only a חטאת and not an עולה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's reason depends on the כהנים eating the meat, and they eat a חטאת but not an עולה. So the word חטאת fits him perfectly. רב יהודה's reason is about the מזבח, and an עולה goes on the מזבח too, so the choice of חטאת looks strange.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense according to (one view)
Why specifically this case?
Sin-offering; the כהנים eat most of it
Burnt-offering; it is burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: Granted, according to Ulla,
that is why it teaches a sin-offering.
But according to Rav Yehuda,
why specifically a sin-offering?
Even a burnt-offering too!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְעוּלָּא הַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי חַטָּאת אֶלָּא לְרַב יְהוּדָה מַאי אִירְיָא חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב יהודה's reason against the specific word חטאת in the teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's explanation that the rule protects the honor of the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the concern is the מזבח, an עולה fits even better, since all of it goes on the מזבח. So limiting the teaching to a חטאת makes no sense for him.

steps.title: It is a 'not only this, but even that' teaching
steps.stepSummary: The teaching is building up. An עולה obviously falls under this concern. The חכמים decreed even for a חטאת, where most of the meat is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is saying 'it is not needed.' It is not needed to say this about an עולה, which is burned completely. But even a חטאת, where only the fat and blood go up to the מזבח and the כהנים eat the rest, even so they decreed it. This is so that people will not say the מזבח eats stolen goods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב יהודה. The teaching picked חטאת on purpose, as the bigger and less obvious case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an עולה, it is obvious that people would say the מזבח eats stolen goods. The whole animal is burned there. The new point is that the חכמים made this decree even for a חטאת, where only a small part reaches the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say (a 'not only, but even' style)
Entirely (burned on the מזבח)
Fat and blood, the parts of a חטאת placed on the מזבח
They made a decree (גזירה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think an עולה is left out of the rule. The teaching names a חטאת only because it is the less obvious case. An עולה is included all the more.

phrases.english: It is saying "it is not necessary":
it is not necessary to say a burnt-offering, which is entirely burned;
but even a sin-offering too,

phrases.aramaic: דְּחֵלֶב וָדָם הוּא דְּסָלֵיק לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: where only the fat and blood go up onto the altar,
and the rest the priests eat;
even so, they decreed,
so that people should not say the altar eats stolen goods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by rereading the wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording as a 'לא מיבעיא' (not only this, but even that) style
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning only a חטאת seemed to leave out an עולה, which goes against רב יהודה's reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חטאת is the bigger new point. If the decree covers even a חטאת, it surely covers an עולה.
steps.whatToRemember: For רב יהודה, the teaching names a חטאת because it is the less obvious case, not because an עולה is left out.

steps.title: The משנה's wording fits עולא, not רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the stolen חטאת that is NOT known does atone. That fits עולא. רב יהודה's focus is the known case, so the משנה should have said the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: about a stolen חטאת that was not known to the public, that it atones, because of the benefit of the מזבח. Granted, according to עולא this works well. But according to רב יהודה, it should have said the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to רב יהודה from the exact wording of the משנה. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states its rule in a positive way: when no one knows, it atones. That matches עולא, whose point is about the unknown case. For רב יהודה, the main rule is that a known theft does NOT atone, so the משנה should have been worded around that case.

keyTerms.meaning: To the public / to many people
The benefit or proper running of the מזבח
It should have said the opposite

phrases.english: We learned:
about a stolen sin-offering
that was not known to the public,
that it atones,
because of the benefit of the altar.
Granted, according to Ulla, it works well;
but according to Rav Yehuda,
it should have said the opposite!
phrases.notes: He means the משנה should have said: if it IS known, it does not atone.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן עַל חַטָּאת הַגְּזוּלָה שֶׁלֹּא נוֹדְעָה לְרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate challenge to רב יהודה, now from how the משנה words its rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that the main point of the enactment is the known case, which does not atone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה states its rule about the unknown case, which atones. That fits עולא's focus. If רב יהודה were right, the משנה would have stated its rule about the known case, which does not atone.

steps.title: The משנה Means Both Sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה really says both things: an unknown stolen חטאת atones, and a known one does not, for the sake of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is also what the משנה is saying: if it is not known, it atones. If it is known, it does not atone, for the benefit of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4. It says the משנה's wording hints at the other side too, and that other side is exactly רב יהודה's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה openly mentions only the unknown case. But that implies the opposite: a known stolen חטאת does not atone. That implied part is רב יהודה's point about protecting the מזבח's reputation, so his reading fits the משנה after all.

keyTerms.meaning: That is also what it is saying (the text includes this meaning too)
It became known (publicly)
It brings atonement
For the good of the מזבח, so that its reputation is protected

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יהודה, the משנה teaches both sides: an unknown stolen חטאת atones, and a known one does not, to protect the מזבח's name.

phrases.english: That is also what it is saying:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה. The גמרא is saying the משנה's words imply the second half too.

phrases.english: if it is not known, it atones,
if it is known, it does not atone,
for the benefit of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4 by reading the משנה as implying the known case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's wording, which implies its opposite case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to speak only about the unknown case, which fits עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה implies both cases, and the known case is רב יהודה's concern for the מזבח.

steps.title: Why Would a Thief Get כרת for Slaughtering Outside?
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a משנה and ברייתא about a thief who made a stolen animal הקדש. If יאוש alone does not give him ownership, his הקדש should not work, so why would he get כרת?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: if someone stole an animal, made it הקדש, and then slaughtered or sold it, he pays double, but not four or five times. And a ברייתא on this says: if he slaughtered it outside the מקדש in such a case, he gets כרת. If you say יאוש alone does not give ownership, why is there כרת?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the idea that the owner's giving up hope (יאוש) is not enough to make a stolen item belong to the thief. He uses a source showing that the thief's הקדש really works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can only make something הקדש if it is his. The ברייתא says the thief gets כרת for slaughtering it outside, so the animal must truly be הקדש. That means the thief owned it, apparently through יאוש alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Double payment that a thief pays
Four- or fivefold payment for slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox
Spiritual cutting off, a heavy Torah punishment
The owner's giving up hope alone, with nothing else changing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two payments. He pays double for the theft. He does not pay four or five times, because when he slaughtered or sold the animal it was already הקדש and no longer counted as the owner's.

phrases.english: Rava raises an objection:
If one stole and consecrated,
and afterward slaughtered or sold it,
he pays double payment,
but does not pay fourfold or fivefold payment.
And it is taught about it:

phrases.aramaic: בַּחוּץ כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא – עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: Outside, in a case like this, he is punished with karet.
phrases.notes: 'Outside' means he slaughtered this הקדש animal outside the מקדש, which is a sin that carries כרת.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ יֵאוּשׁ כְּדִי לָא קָנֵי,
phrases.english: And if you say that despair alone does not acquire,
phrases.notes: כדי here means 'by itself': the owner gave up hope, but nothing else happened to the animal.

phrases.english: what is karet doing here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה's wording to the basic premise that יאוש alone does not give ownership.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's position, that יאוש alone does not let the thief acquire the stolen item. This is why, for him, by Torah law a stolen חטאת does not atone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כרת for slaughtering outside shows the הקדש worked. הקדש only works on what a person owns, so the thief must have owned the animal through יאוש.

steps.title: רב שיזבי: כרת by Rabbinic Law
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי answers that the כרת comes 'from their words', from the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said: it is כרת from their words.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי answers רבא's question with a short, surprising phrase: this כרת is 'מדבריהם', from the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that by Torah law alone the thief would not own the animal. The כרת exists only because of something the חכמים did, and רבא explains what that is in Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: From their words, meaning from the חכמים

phrases.english: Rav Sheizevi said:
Karet by their words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Credits the result to a decision of the חכמים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כרת shows that יאוש alone gives ownership by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כרת is there because of the חכמים, not because יאוש alone gives ownership.

steps.title: They Laugh: Can כרת Be Rabbinic?
steps.stepSummary: The listeners laugh at רב שיזבי, because כרת is a Torah punishment and the חכמים cannot create it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at him: is there such a thing as כרת from the חכמים?!
steps.whatsHappening: The people listening mock רב שיזבי's answer. To them, 'rabbinic כרת' sounds impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כרת is a punishment from Heaven that only the Torah sets. The challenge is that the חכמים cannot invent it, so the answer seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: They laughed at him
Is there such a thing? (a sharp question)

phrases.english: They laughed at him:
Is there such a thing as karet by rabbinic law?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב שיזבי's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the Torah can set כרת. The חכמים cannot create a Heavenly punishment.

steps.title: רבא Explains: The Sages Gave Him Ownership
steps.stepSummary: רבא defends רב שיזבי. The חכמים treated the animal as the thief's own, so his הקדש works and the כרת follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to them: a great man said something, do not laugh at it. He means כרת that comes to him through the words of the חכמים. The חכמים placed the animal in his possession so that he would be liable for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains what רב שיזבי meant. The חכמים did not create כרת. They created the ownership, and the Torah's כרת follows from that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים decided to treat the stolen animal as the thief's. Because of that, his הקדש works, and slaughtering it outside brings real Torah כרת. So the ברייתא does not prove that יאוש alone gives ownership by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man
Through their words, caused by the חכמים
They placed it in his possession (ownership)

steps.whatToRemember: 'כרת מדבריהם' means the חכמים gave the thief ownership, and that ownership leads to a real Torah כרת.

phrases.english: Rava said to them:
A great man said something,
do not laugh at it;

phrases.aramaic: כָּרֵת שֶׁעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵיהֶן בָּאתָה לוֹ –
phrases.english: it is karet that came to him through their words:
phrases.notes: The כרת itself is from the Torah. The חכמים only set up the situation that leads to it.

phrases.english: the Rabbis placed it in his possession
so that he would be liable for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רָבָא: גַּבְרָא רַבָּה אָמַר מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the mockery in Step 8 by explaining רב שיזבי's words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the mechanism: a rabbinic transfer of ownership that triggers a Torah punishment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Rabbinic כרת' means the חכמים invented a כרת punishment.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים gave the thief ownership, so the Torah's כרת applies to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers רבא's objection in Step 6, so the view that יאוש alone does not give ownership by Torah law still stands.

steps.title: From When Did the Animal Become His?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether the חכמים gave the thief ownership from the time of the theft or from the time of the הקדש. The practical difference is the wool and the offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this is a real question for me. When the חכמים placed it in his possession, was it from the time of the theft or from the time of the הקדש? What difference does it make? For its wool and its offspring. What is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the חכמים gave the thief ownership, רבא asks when that ownership began. He also explains why it matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ownership began at the theft, the wool and offspring that came between the theft and the הקדש would belong to the thief. If it began at the הקדש, those belong to the original owner and must be returned.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a question (unsolved problem) for me
From the time of the theft
From the time it was made הקדש
What practical difference does it make?
Wool shearings and offspring

phrases.english: Rava said:
This is certainly a question for me:
when the Rabbis placed it in his possession,
was it from the time of the theft or from the time of its consecration?
What difference does it make?
For its wool and its offspring.
What is the answer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 9's idea that the חכמים gave the thief ownership, and asks when it began.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rabbinic ownership begins at the theft or at the הקדש

steps.title: From the Consecration, So the Sinner Will Not Profit
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers his own question: ownership begins at the הקדש, so the thief will not gain from his sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then רבא said: it makes sense that it is from the time of the הקדש, so that the sinner does not profit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. The thief's ownership starts only from the הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים gave the thief ownership only to make him liable. If ownership began at the theft, he would keep the wool and offspring and gain from stealing. So it begins at the הקדש, and those extras go back to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said (answering his own question)
It makes sense, it stands to reason
So that the sinner should not profit

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים made the thief the owner from the time of the הקדש, not from the theft, so that he cannot keep the wool or offspring and profit from his sin.

phrases.english: Rava then said:
It stands to reason that it is from the time of its consecration,
so that the sinner not profit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Ownership begins at the הקדש, so that the sinner will not profit.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ownership the חכמים gave the thief starts at the הקדש. The wool and offspring from before that go back to the owner.

steps.title: When the law of סיקריקון applied in Judea
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a new topic. The special law of סיקריקון did not apply during the time of the war killings, and it did apply from then on.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The law of the extortionist did not apply in יהודה during the time when people were being killed in the war. From the war killings and onward, the law of the extortionist did apply there.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, and it opens a brand-new topic: land taken by a violent extortionist, called a סיקריקון. It first tells us when the special law about such land was in force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets a time limit on the law. During the war period the law did not apply, and after that period it did. The משנה has not yet told us what the law is; the next line, starting with כיצד, will spell it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
A violent extortionist who took land from its owner by threats
The time when people were being killed in the war

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the previous discussion about the thief and his הקדש. This is a completely new משנה with a new topic.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The law of the extortionist did not apply in Judea
during the time of those killed in the war.
From the war killings and onward,
the law of the extortionist applied there.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הָיָה סִיקָרִיקוֹן בִּיהוּדָה בַּהֲרוּגֵי מִלְחָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and topic after the discussion of the thief's הקדש is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law of סיקריקון was not in force during the war killings. It was in force from then on.

steps.title: The order of buying decides whether the sale holds
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the law. If the buyer bought from the extortionist first and then from the owner, his purchase is void. If he bought from the owner first and then from the extortionist, his purchase stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If someone bought a field from the extortionist and then went back and bought it from the owner, his purchase is void. If he bought from the owner first and then went back and bought from the extortionist, his purchase stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks 'how so?' and then explains what the law of סיקריקון actually is. It turns on the order in which the buyer bought the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the buyer has bought from the extortionist, the owner's later sale is not taken as a real sale, because the owner can say he did not truly mean to sell. If the buyer goes to the owner first, the משנה rules that the sale stands.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? It introduces an explanation of the rule just stated
The original owner of the field
His purchase is void
His purchase stands

steps.confusionAlert: Both purchases involve the same field and the same buyer. The only difference between the two cases is which seller he went to first.

phrases.english: How so?
If one bought from the extortionist,
and then went back and bought from the owner,
his purchase is void.
If he bought from the owner first,
and then went back and bought from the extortionist –
his purchase stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the law of סיקריקון mentioned in step 12 actually is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buying from the extortionist first and then from the owner makes the purchase void. Buying from the owner first and then from the extortionist makes it stand.

steps.title: The same pattern with a husband and wife
steps.stepSummary: Buying a wife's field from the husband first and then from the wife makes the purchase void. Buying from the wife first and then from the husband makes it stand. This was the original version of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone bought from the husband and then went back and bought from the wife, his purchase is void. If he bought from the wife first and then from the husband, his purchase stands. This is the original version of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second case that works the same way, involving a field that belongs to a wife. Then it says that everything so far was the original version of the law, which tells us that a change is coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the husband has already sold, the wife can say she only agreed so as not to fight with him. So her sale does not count. If the buyer asks her first, her agreement is real. The words זו משנה ראשונה signal that later courts changed the law, and the next steps show how.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the husband, who has rights to use his wife's field
Here: the wife, who owns the field itself
The original, earlier version of the law, later changed

phrases.english: If one bought from the husband
phrases.notes: He is buying the husband's rights in a field that belongs to the wife.

phrases.english: and then went back and bought from the wife –
his purchase is void.

phrases.aramaic: מִן הָאִשָּׁה וְחָזַר וְלָקַח מִן הָאִישׁ –
phrases.english: If he bought from the wife and then went back and bought from the husband –
his purchase stands.
This is the original version of the law.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָקַח מִן הָאִישׁ וְחָזַר וְלָקַח מִן הָאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case that follows the same order-of-purchase logic as step 13, then labels all of it as the original law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Husband first and then wife makes the purchase void. Wife first and then husband makes it stand. These rules belong to the משנה ראשונה.

steps.title: A later court: the buyer pays the owner a quarter
steps.stepSummary: A later בית דין ruled that whoever buys from the extortionist must give the owner a quarter. This applies only when the owner cannot buy the field himself. If he can, he comes before everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court that came after them said: one who buys from the extortionist gives the owners a quarter. When is that? When the owners are not able to buy it themselves. But if they are able to buy it, they come before anyone else.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now tells us how a later בית דין changed the original law. A purchase from the extortionist can now hold, but the buyer must pay the owner a quarter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the original law, buying from the extortionist first was simply void. The later court lets the sale stand, but it protects the owner in two ways. He receives a quarter, and if he has the means, he gets the first right to buy back his own field.

keyTerms.meaning: The court that came after them, a later generation of חכמים
A quarter
The original owners
Come first, have the first right

phrases.english: The court of those who came after them said:
One who buys from the extortionist
gives the owners a quarter.
When does this apply?
When they are not able to buy it,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the original owners, who cannot afford to buy the field back.

phrases.english: but if they are able to buy it –
they come before anyone else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the original rule from steps 13 and 14 with a new arrangement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A purchase from the extortionist stands, but the buyer gives the owner a quarter. If the owner can afford to buy, he has the first right.

steps.title: רבי's court: after twelve months, anyone may buy
steps.stepSummary: רבי's בית דין voted that once the field has been with the extortionist for twelve months, whoever buys first acquires it. He must still give the owner a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי set up a court and they voted: if the field stayed in the extortionist's hands for twelve months, whoever buys it first acquires it, but he gives the owners a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the final stage of the law, decided by a vote in רבי's court. After twelve months with the extortionist, the field is open for anyone to buy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier court gave the owner the first right to buy. רבי's court adds a time limit: after twelve months the owner loses that first right, and the first buyer wins the field. The owner is still protected by receiving a quarter.

keyTerms.meaning: They counted votes, decided by a vote
It remained, meaning the field stayed in his hands
He acquires it

steps.whatToRemember: There are three stages. First, the original law depended on the order of buying. Second, a later court let the sale stand but had the buyer give the owner a quarter, with the owner having the first right to buy. Third, רבי's court ruled that after twelve months anyone may buy first, still giving the owner a quarter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the חכמים adjusting the law in stages, trying to balance protecting the robbed owner with letting land be bought and sold.

phrases.english: רבי convened a court and they voted
that if the field remained before the extortionist
phrases.notes: 'Before' here means in his hands, in his possession.

phrases.english: for twelve months,
whoever buys it first acquires it;
but he gives the owners a quarter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a twelve-month time limit to the later court's ruling from step 15, and removes the owner's first right after that time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After twelve months with the extortionist, the first buyer acquires the field and gives the owner a quarter.

steps.title: Challenging the משנה's Timeline
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how it could be that there was no סיקריקון during the war killings, yet there was סיקריקון afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Now, if during the time of the war killings there was no סיקריקון, is it possible that from the war killings onward there was סיקריקון?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה by attacking its wording. It sounds backwards: if anything, extortion should have been worse during the war, not after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the משנה says there were no extortionists during the war but there were afterward. That makes no sense, because violent seizing of land fits wartime best. The גמרא is pushing for a better reading of the משנה's words.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא section, which discusses the משנה
Now; used here to mean 'if this is so, then…'
The war killings; the period of the war against Rome
An extortionist who takes land by threat; also the special law about buying land from him
And onward; from then on

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Now, if in the time of the war killings
there was no סיקריקון in it (in יהודה),
then from the war killings and onward,
there is סיקריקון in it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא בַּהֲרוּגֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה לֹא הָיָה בָּהּ סִיקָרִיקוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's first line from Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that there was no סיקריקון during the war killings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Extortion would be more likely during the war than after it, so the plain reading cannot be right.

steps.title: רב יהודה Rereads the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the משנה means the courts did not apply the law of סיקריקון during the war, not that there were no extortionists.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The משנה is saying, 'they did not apply the law of סיקריקון to it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the challenge by changing how we read the משנה. There were extortionists during the war, but the special law about them was not used then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of סיקריקון says a purchase from the extortionist is void. רב יהודה says this rule was not applied during the war, so purchases from extortionists then were valid. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: They judged; the courts ruled
Law; legal ruling
It is saying; this is what the text means

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying there were no extortionists during the war. It means the courts did not use the special rule that cancels purchases from them, so those purchases stood.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
It is saying, "they did not apply the law of סיקריקון to it."

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא דָּנוּ בָּהּ דִּין סִיקָרִיקוֹן קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say there were no extortionists during the war.
steps.terutzMaskana: There were extortionists, but the law that cancels purchases from them was not applied during the war.

steps.title: רבי אסי's Three Decrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי reports three decrees about killing Jews: kill or be killed, then a fine of four זוזים for killing, then death for killing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אסי said: They issued three decrees. The first decree: whoever does not kill a Jew should be killed. The middle one: whoever kills should pay four זוזים. The last one: whoever kills should be killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אסי's report to back up רב יהודה. It lists three decrees in order, preparing for the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first two decrees, a non-Jew could kill a Jew with no real penalty. Under the last decree, killing a Jew meant death. This change is what decides whether a sale to an extortionist was real.

keyTerms.meaning: Decrees
The first one
The middle one
The last one
Zuz coins

phrases.english: As Rabbi Asi said:
They issued three decrees.
phrases.notes: "They" means the non-Jewish rulers during and after the war.

phrases.english: The first decree:
anyone who does not kill a Jew, let them kill him.
The middle one:
anyone who kills should bring four zuz.
The last one:
anyone who kills, let them kill him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי שָׁלֹשׁ גְּזֵירוֹת גָּזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the background that supports רב יהודה's reading in Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's claim that the law of סיקריקון was not applied during the war.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אסי's report of the three decrees about killing Jews.

steps.title: Why the Sale Counts Only Under the First Two Decrees
steps.stepSummary: Under the first two decrees the owner truly gave up his field to save his life. Under the last decree he planned to sue later, so he never truly gave it up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, under the first and middle decrees, since they would kill, the owner fully decided to transfer the field because of the danger to his life. Under the last decree, owners would say: 'Let him take it for now; tomorrow I will sue him in court.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the three decrees to explain רב יהודה's reading. It shows why sales to extortionists were valid during the war but void afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the extortionist could kill without punishment, the owner gave the field away wholeheartedly to save himself, so the sale was real. Once killing a Jew meant death, the owner felt safe enough to plan a lawsuit, so he never truly let go. That is when the law of סיקריקון applies and a purchase from the extortionist is void.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
His duress; the force or danger he faced
He fully decides and transfers ownership
I will claim; I will sue
In court

steps.whatToRemember: The law of סיקריקון depends on whether the owner truly let go of his field. Under deadly threat with no penalty for the killer, he let go fully and the sale stands. Once killers were punished, he expected to win in court, so he never let go and purchases from the extortionist are void.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the whole law of סיקריקון in the משנה. A forced sale is judged by whether the owner, inside himself, really transferred the field.

phrases.english: Therefore, under the first and the middle decrees,
since they would kill,
because of his duress he fully decides and transfers it.
Under the last decree, they say:
"For now, let him take it;
tomorrow I will claim it from him in court."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אסי's decrees from Step 19 to explain רב יהודה's reading in Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: During the war, sales to extortionists stood because the owner truly let go. After the war, the owner planned to sue, so the law of סיקריקון makes purchases from the extortionist void.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן on Three Destructions
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses a פסוק about fear and hard-heartedness to introduce three destructions: ירושלים, טור מלכא and ביתר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: What is the meaning of the פסוק, 'Happy is the man who fears always, but one who hardens his heart will fall into evil'? Because of קמצא and בר קמצא, ירושלים was destroyed. Because of a rooster and a hen, טור מלכא was destroyed. Because of the shaft of a chariot, ביתר was destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the law of סיקריקון to a new aggadic section about the war against Rome. רבי יוחנן names three disasters that each began with something small, which the stories coming next will explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן ties these destructions to the פסוק in משלי about fear and a hardened heart. Each one grew out of a small-sounding cause: a mix-up between two people, a pair of birds, a chariot part. This step is only the heading, and the details come next.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written
Fears always; is always careful
Hardens his heart
Was destroyed
The King's Mountain, a region in ארץ ישראל
ביתר, the city destroyed after the בר כוכבא revolt

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Happy is the man who fears always,
but one who hardens his heart will fall into evil"?
On account of Kamtza and Bar Kamtza, Jerusalem was destroyed;
on account of a rooster and a hen, the King's Mountain was destroyed;
on account of the shaft of a chariot, Beitar was destroyed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי דִּכְתִיב אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם מְפַחֵד תָּמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the halachic discussion of סיקריקון and opens an aggadic section about the war and the destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three great destructions (ירושלים, טור מלכא, ביתר) each began with a small cause, as hinted by the פסוק about fear and a hardened heart.

steps.title: ירושלים destroyed because of קמצא and בר קמצא: the invitation mix-up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says ירושלים was destroyed because of קמצא and בר קמצא. It starts the story: a host told his servant to bring his friend קמצא, and the servant brought his enemy בר קמצא instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירושלים was destroyed because of קמצא and בר קמצא. There was a man whose friend was קמצא and whose enemy was בר קמצא. He made a feast and told his servant, 'Go bring me קמצא.' The servant went and brought him בר קמצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the first of רבי יוחנן's three destructions, ירושלים, by naming its cause and opening the story. It sets the scene for the confrontation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening line tells us the ending first: ירושלים was destroyed. Then it goes back to a small, personal beginning, a servant mixing up two similar names. The mistake puts the host's enemy at his party.

keyTerms.meaning: The host's friend
The host's enemy
His enemy
A feast
His servant

steps.confusionAlert: קמצא (the friend) and בר קמצא (the enemy) are two different people with almost the same name. The whole mix-up comes from that.

phrases.english: On account of Kamtza and bar Kamtza, Jerusalem was destroyed –
for there was a certain man whose friend was Kamtza,
and whose enemy was bar Kamtza.
He made a feast,
and said to his servant:
Go bring me Kamtza.
He went and brought him bar Kamtza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the first destruction (ירושלים) that רבי יוחנן listed in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירושלים was destroyed because of קמצא and בר קמצא. The story begins when a servant brings the host's enemy to his feast by mistake.

steps.title: The host orders בר קמצא out, and בר קמצא offers to pay
steps.stepSummary: The host finds בר קמצא sitting at the feast and tells him to leave because they are enemies. בר קמצא asks to stay and offers to pay for whatever he eats and drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: The host came and found him sitting there. He said to him, 'You are my enemy. What do you want here? Get up and leave!' בר קמצא said, 'Since I already came, let me stay, and I will pay you for whatever I eat and drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the host confronts בר קמצא, and בר קמצא tries to avoid being thrown out. The argument keeps building in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The host speaks indirectly ('that man is the enemy of that man') but his meaning is clear: you are my enemy. בר קמצא does not argue about the feud. He only wants to avoid being sent out in front of everyone, so he offers to pay his own way.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all
Get up, leave
Since I have already come
Leave me be, let me stay

phrases.english: He came and found him sitting there.
phrases.notes: The host is the one who came, and he found בר קמצא already seated.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי הָהוּא גַּבְרָא בְּעֵל דְּבָבֵאּ דְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא הוּא,
phrases.english: Since that man is the enemy of that man,
phrases.notes: This is a roundabout way of saying 'you are my enemy.'

phrases.english: What do you want here? Get up and leave!
He said to him: Since I have already come,
let me stay, and I will give you
the cost of whatever I eat and drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 22 now that בר קמצא is at the feast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The host demands that בר קמצא leave. בר קמצא pleads to stay and offers to pay for his food and drink so he will not be embarrassed.
